junction.name: Polk Street & Eddy Street, San Francisco

claims.text: Polk Street & Eddy Street had 17 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Polk Street & Eddy Street's own: the city's record places 34 of the 51 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.2 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2019. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.5 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $175,000 a year.
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.1 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $36,000 a year.
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for Eddy Street, Polk Street, Willow Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.
